findings.title: Reference physical schema covers only 30 of 74 catalog tables
findings.evidence: 30 CREATE TABLE definitions exist; 44 catalog tables have no reference DDL.
findings.risk: A freeze candidate cannot be deeply checked for keys, tenant isolation, lifecycle constraints, indexes, immutability or transaction support across all frozen aggregate roots.
findings.required_fix: Produce complete v0.2 reference DDL/logical column model for all 74 tables, even if production migrations remain later.

findings.title: Owned-child foreign keys do not consistently enforce tenant agreement
findings.evidence: Examples include item_barcodes→items, inventory_bucket_positions→inventory_positions, sale_lines→sales, payment attempts/commitments/tenders→checkout_payments, return lines/obligations→sales_returns, credit ledger→credit_accounts and cash movements→shifts using parent ID alone while the child also stores tenant_id.
findings.risk: A malformed/buggy write can persist tenant_id=A on a child whose parent belongs to tenant B. Global UUID uniqueness does not prove tenant equality.
findings.required_fix: For every tenant-bearing owned relationship, either use composite tenant-scoped FK `(tenant_id,parent_id)` to a matching UNIQUE key, or remove redundant child tenant_id and derive tenant through the parent. Document one consistent rule.

findings.title: Database decision-seam treatment is not traceable to all 60 frozen Decision IDs
findings.evidence: Frozen Domain Model contains 60 non-resolved/verification Decision IDs; the database treatment document explicitly cites only 0 IDs.
findings.risk: Conceptual prose cannot prove that every OPEN/PROPOSED/VERIFY/DEFERRED seam survived physical design without accidental resolution.
findings.required_fix: Create a 60/60 Decision-ID matrix with database columns/constraints/indexes/migrations affected and an explicit 'not resolved here' treatment.

findings.title: Physical transaction specification is incomplete versus the frozen posting-envelope matrix
findings.evidence: Detailed database flows exist for Sale, Goods Receipt, Sales Return, Refund and generic credit/Stock Count, but Purchase Return, Customer Collection, Supplier Payment, Financial receipt/payment, Account Transfer, Expense and Manual cash-in/out lack equivalent lock/revalidation/write/source-uniqueness sequences.
findings.risk: The most important cross-context atomicity guarantee can diverge by implementation path.
findings.required_fix: Define all 13 frozen local posting envelopes with exact lock roots/order, revalidation, immutable facts, maintained balances, Audit, Outbox and idempotency behavior.

findings.title: Cumulative Sales/Purchase return eligibility has no concrete PostgreSQL serialization mechanism
findings.evidence: v0.1 says to acquire source consistency keys/advisory guards and scan posted return facts, but does not define whether the source line is row-locked, which advisory key is used, or how two concurrent returns are serialized.
findings.risk: Two counters can both observe remaining returnable quantity and over-return the same SaleLine/GRNLine.
findings.required_fix: Choose a physical serialization strategy that does not change business policy: e.g. `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` on immutable source line solely as a mutex, or transaction-scoped advisory lock derived from tenant+source-line identity; then query cumulative effective returns under that lock.

findings.title: Maintained balances lack complete database reconciliation invariants
findings.evidence: InventoryPosition/on_hand, bucket positions, CreditAccount.outstanding, CashierShift.expected_cash and FinancialAccount.current_balance are maintained beside immutable ledgers, but v0.1 does not specify authoritative equations, drift detection, rebuild rules or same-source uniqueness for each.
findings.risk: A crash/bug/migration can leave current balances inconsistent with immutable facts while both appear valid.
findings.required_fix: Define invariant equations, update source identity, reconciliation queries, repair policy and acceptance tests for Inventory, Credit, Cash and Financial balances. Explicitly define `on_hand = Σ bucket quantities` where buckets are active.

findings.title: Idempotency and inbox deduplication transaction semantics are not sufficiently precise
findings.evidence: A unique idempotency key exists, but v0.1 does not define claim/in-progress/completed race handling or fingerprint mismatch behavior. Inbox receipt is described as 'before/with' application rather than explicitly committed atomically with the applied incoming effect.
findings.risk: Concurrent retries can race; a crash can record a message without applying it or apply it without durable dedup evidence.
findings.required_fix: Specify idempotency state machine and locking/insert-on-conflict behavior; require inbox receipt + incoming business effect + resulting outbox/audit to commit in the same transaction.

findings.title: `numeric(24,8)` is selected without documented capacity proof
findings.evidence: The type is consistently proposed, but maximum document totals, cumulative balances, quantities, WAC and intermediate multiplication/division bounds are not proven.
findings.risk: Rare large values or intermediate calculations can overflow/round unexpectedly despite using exact decimal.
findings.required_fix: Create a precision budget per value class and boundary tests; widen types if necessary. Legal/display rounding remains CountryRuleSet policy.

findings.title: Append-only protection is described but not physically specified
findings.evidence: v0.1 mentions repository permissions/status-aware predicates/trigger protection, while reference DDL contains no immutable-table UPDATE/DELETE guard strategy.
findings.risk: A defect or support script could rewrite stock, tender, credit, cash, financial or audit history.
findings.required_fix: Specify DB role privileges and/or immutable triggers for high-risk ledger/fact tables, with an explicit controlled migration/repair path.

findings.title: Outbox publisher claim/lease behavior is unspecified
findings.evidence: Pending index and retry fields exist, but no `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`, lease/claim, worker ownership or crash-after-publish behavior is defined.
findings.risk: Multiple workers may duplicate work or stall rows. At-least-once behavior is not explicit.
findings.required_fix: Define outbox dispatch concurrency and at-least-once semantics; rely on event ID/inbox dedup for duplicate delivery.

findings.title: Moving-WAC physical update and audit evidence are under-specified
findings.evidence: GRN says update WAC and stock movements store unit_cost/value_delta, but prior/new quantity/value/WAC derivation, zero-stock reset behavior and deterministic discount/tax acquisition allocation evidence are not fully specified.
findings.risk: Costing may be correct operationally but difficult to reproduce/reconcile after failure or migration.
findings.required_fix: Define WAC transaction formula inputs, stored evidence and reconciliation query, including free quantity, allocated discounts, recoverable/non-recoverable tax classification and purchase-return treatment.

findings.title: Tender/refund materialization uniqueness is incomplete
findings.evidence: `posted_tenders` uniquely constrains nullable `payment_commitment_id`; manual/cash paths and RefundExecution/RefundObligation linkage are not yet physically complete because relevant catalog tables are absent from reference DDL.
findings.risk: A retry may materialize duplicate settlement facts on paths without a non-null commitment.
findings.required_fix: Define a non-null logical settlement source identity/idempotency key for every PostedTender and refund settlement path.

findings.title: Index strategy is illustrative rather than workload-complete
findings.evidence: Only core examples are listed; the 74-table model has no query-to-index matrix for barcode, item search, document lookup, event search, allocations, reconciliation, sync and posting locks.
findings.risk: Correctness may survive but Phase-1 performance targets and lock efficiency may fail at realistic volume.
findings.required_fix: Create query/index coverage matrix with expected cardinality/selectivity and EXPLAIN/benchmark acceptance targets.

findings.title: Cross-schema migration ordering and application/schema compatibility contract need concrete design
findings.evidence: Expand/contract is stated, but 15-schema dependency ordering, migration lock, partially applied migration recovery and Store Node startup compatibility range are not specified.
findings.risk: Interrupted upgrades can leave a store unable to trade or allow incompatible code to write.
findings.required_fix: Define migration ledger/lock, module dependency order, transactional vs non-transactional migration rules, compatibility range and recovery procedure.

findings.title: Frozen lifecycle constraints are not enumerated table-by-table
findings.evidence: Status is mostly `varchar(40)` and the model says CHECK constraints should be used 'where frozen', but there is no authoritative status/transition constraint matrix.
findings.risk: Persistence can accept impossible states even when the Domain Model has frozen lifecycle rules.
findings.required_fix: Create lifecycle persistence matrix: allowed stored states, required companion timestamps/amounts, transition enforcement location and invariants for Sale, payment attempts/commitments, Return, RefundObligation/Execution, shifts, BusinessDay and procurement documents.
